pr_title: importccl: Use column ids when importing data.
pr_body:
Previously, import processors used column names when
identifying which columns to import the data into.

This is problematic because column names might contain
special characters and need to be quoted.  We thus would
fail to find a matching column in the table descriptor,
resulting in an error.

Instead of using column names, use column IDs, which removes
the need to worry about quoting.

Release notes (bug fix): Correctly handle columns named with
reserved keywords.

issue_context.title: IMPORT INTO has problems with quoted identifiers
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

I'm attempting to migrate some data over from an SQLite intermediary format and having trouble with `IMPORT INTO` tripping up over a column it says doesn't exist:

```
root@localhost:26257/cpsasurvey> IMPORT INTO "cpsasurvey"."gradedSurveys" ("id", "timestamp", "graderId", "responseId", "flags", "gradingTime", "scrollCount", "remoteJobId")
    CSV DATA ('http://localhost:9001/cpsasurvey.gradedSurveys.csv');
pq: verifying target columns: column "\"timestamp\"" does not exist
root@localhost:26257/cpsasurvey>
root@localhost:26257/cpsasurvey> show columns from "gradedSurveys";
  column_name | data_type | is_nullable | column_default | generation_expression |                                                                                                    indices                                                                                                    | is_hidden
+-------------+-----------+-------------+----------------+-----------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+
  id          | STRING    |    false    | NULL           |                       | {pK_gradedSurveys,gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Graders_graderId,gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Responses_responseId,iX_gradedSurveys_responseId,iX_gradedSurveys_graderId_responseId} |   false
  timestamp   | INT8      |    false    | NULL           |                       | {}                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   false
  graderId    | STRING    |    false    | NULL           |                       | {gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Graders_graderId,iX_gradedSurveys_graderId_responseId}                                                                                                             |   false
  remoteJobId | STRING    |    true     | NULL           |                       | {}                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   false
  responseId  | STRING    |    false    | NULL           |                       | {gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Responses_responseId,iX_gradedSurveys_responseId,iX_gradedSurveys_graderId_responseId}                                                                             |   false
  flags       | INT8      |    false    | NULL           |                       | {}                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   false
  gradingTime | FLOAT8    |    false    | NULL           |                       | {}                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   false
  scrollCount | INT8      |    false    | NULL           |                       | {}                                                                                                                                                                                                            |   false
(8 rows)

Time: 21.412ms
```

Two thoughts:

* `"timestamp"` is being treated as a reserved keyword rather than as a column name, despite being quoted?
* it seems from the output that the literal `"` used to "special-case" the reserved keyword `timestamp` may be treated as part of the column name? (note the escaped `\"` within the outer quotes in the error message)

I altered the table to temporarily rename `timestamp` to `tstamp` and tried again, this time it threw an error on `"graderId"`, confirming the second point above:

```
root@localhost:26257/cpsasurvey> IMPORT INTO "cpsasurvey"."gradedSurveys" ("id", "tstamp", "graderId", "responseId", flags, "gradingTime", "scrollCount", "remoteJobId")
    CSV DATA ('http://localhost:9001/cpsasurvey.gradedSurveys.csv');
pq: verifying target columns: column "\"graderId\"" does not exist
```

I thought perhaps the bug was that columns were being treated as literal values (no quoting *and* no case-folding), and tried with `graderId` rather than `"graderId"` but the error confirmed that it's not the case: case-folding *is* performed but double-quoting is *not* accounted for:


```
root@localhost:26257/cpsasurvey> IMPORT INTO "cpsasurvey"."gradedSurveys" (id, tstamp, graderId, responseId, flags, gradingTime, scrollCount, remoteJobId)
    CSV DATA ('http://localhost:9001/cpsasurvey.gradedSurveys.csv');
pq: verifying target columns: column "graderid" does not exist
```

So the real problem is that the code is entirely unaware of the semantics of double quotes altogether.

(I have the explicit column names in the query as the order differs from the `.dump` output of `sqlite3`, but I believe it's a bug even if I didn't need to reorder the data, no? So long as `IMPORT INTO` has the option of taking column names, I believe it should respect the same naming rules and quoting formats as the rest of the SQL commands.)


**To Reproduce**

Started a new single-node cluster in insecure mode and created the following table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE "gradedSurveys" (
	id STRING NOT NULL,
	"timestamp" INT8 NOT NULL,
	"graderId" STRING NOT NULL,
	"remoteJobId" STRING NULL,
	"responseId" STRING NOT NULL,
	flags INT8 NOT NULL,
	"gradingTime" FLOAT8 NOT NULL,
	"scrollCount" INT8 NOT NULL,
	/*CONSTRAINT "pK_gradedSurveys" PRIMARY KEY (id ASC),
	CONSTRAINT "fK_gradedSurveys_Graders_graderId" FOREIGN KEY ("graderId") REFERENCES graders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
	CONSTRAINT "fK_gradedSurveys_Responses_responseId" FOREIGN KEY ("responseId") REFERENCES responses(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
	INDEX "gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Graders_graderId" ("graderId" ASC),
	INDEX "gradedSurveys_auto_index_fK_gradedSurveys_Responses_responseId" ("responseId" ASC),
	INDEX "iX_gradedSurveys_responseId" ("responseId" ASC),
	UNIQUE INDEX "iX_gradedSurveys_graderId_responseId" ("graderId" ASC, "responseId" ASC),
	FAMILY "primary" (id, tstamp, "graderId", "remoteJobId", "responseId", flags, "gradingTime", "scrollCount")*/
);
```

then executed the import statement above at the cli. 

**Expected behavior**
The quoted column name should be used as-is and found.

**Additional data / screenshots**

**Environment:**
 - CockroachDB version: 19.2.4
 - Server OS: Windows 10 1909
 - Client app: `cockroach sql`

EDIT: note that there was no problem with the quoted identifiers for the database and table names.
comments: Thank you for this detailed report.  I can confirm the symptoms you've observed.  Don't have an eta yet for the fix since it might be more involved than originally though.

review_comments: could we just change `name.String()` to `active.Name` rather than switch everything to IDs right now?
I tried doing that... The entire pipeline was getting stuck anyway.  We would need to re-resolve the names because we serialize those names into the proto.

right, we serialize the names, but my suggestion is we should be serializing `columnDesc.Name`, which is exactly the same string we'll compare to on the other end, right? so then whatever quotes or whatnot are in the name itself are in our string, but we don't really care -- it is just some string to us at that point?
